{{ block title }}Task 1 - Instructions{{ endblock }} {{ block content }}

Think of a number between 1 to 6 (that is, any number among 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), and remember it. We call it “your number chosen”.

On the next page, the computer will randomly draw a number between 1 to 6 for you, each with equal chance. We call it “computer’s number chosen”.

We will then ask you to report whether the computer’s number chosen is the same as your number chosen. If yes, you will receive a payoff of GBP 1.00; if no, you will receive nothing.

In addition, you have been randomly put into a four-person group with three other participants of this experiment. After all four of you make your “yes/no” report, each will be given a rank in your group based on your existing payoff from that report (ties are resolved by a random draw), so your rank will be either 1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th. The person ranked 1st in your group will get an additional payoff of GBP 1.00, and the three others get no additional payoff. In other words, if your rank is 1st in your group, you will receive an additional GBP 1.00 on top of the payoff from your report; if your rank is 2nd, 3rd or 4th in your group, you only receive the payoff from your report.

Note that this is a one-time decision.

Now please think of a number between 1 to 6. Once you are done, please click “Next” to proceed. You will see “computer’s number chosen” on the next page.
